title: Compare compatibility shims with the supported reference API and version
applies_when: A compatibility shim or backport is compared with a similarly named API, or compatibility restoration assumes old-release acceptance is a supported promise; examples include TensorRT-LLM hf_parameter_utils getters, Zipp Path.relative_to and Pluggy class-valued hookspecs.
lesson: First identify which upstream API is actually promised, then resolve its supported revision and current maintainer intent before designing the expected result. A Path-like interface is not a promise to duplicate every pathlib.Path behavior: Zipp names zipfile.Path as its backport reference. Its relative_to and the native CPython 3.14.3 zipfile.Path both return a string and allow parent traversal; a two-case native comparison agrees for child and nonchild paths. This refutes a mismatch premise, not all possible defects. Likewise, TensorRT-LLM's parameter-only getters match Transformers 5.5.4 ModuleUtilsMixin device/dtype properties, including StopIteration for buffer-only modules. A test demanding buffer fallback therefore does not establish the claimed upstream mismatch. Pluggy #794 is a different counterexample: old-version acceptance and a real downstream failure were reproduced, but maintainers explicitly rejected class-valued hookspec restoration as an unintended use and directed the fix downstream. More passing restoration tests cannot decide API intent. Read the latest issue/PR disposition before implementing or publishing; stop the rejected premise rather than equating a behavior delta with an upstream defect. Check both the boundary and a normal control against unchanged reference code; label AST-extracted getter checks as component evidence, not whole-package qualification. If broader behavior is independently required by a supported contract, propose that change on its own merits.
avoid_when: Matching the pinned reference does not prove either implementation meets every caller's needs. A shared upstream defect can still warrant a change. Other dependency versions, overridden properties, quantized module representations and actual model paths need separate evidence. Do not reject a real public API defect solely because internal callers omit the boundary, or claim measured PR-conversion gains from this source counterexample.

evidence.note: The reviewed consumer revision pins transformers==5.5.4; an older implementation is not automatically its compatibility reference.
The shim explicitly targets Transformers v5 ModuleUtilsMixin behavior and its getters inspect parameters only.

Transformers 5.5.4's actual device and dtype properties use the same parameter-only behavior. These pinned sources disprove a buffer-fallback compatibility-mismatch premise; they do not establish full-model correctness.

The project explicitly describes itself as the official backport of zipfile.Path and says to use Zipp Path in its place. This identifies the comparison API, not an unconditional promise of every pathlib method or behavior.

Path.relative_to delegates to posixpath.relpath. An independent native Windows CPython3.14.3 two-case check against its installed zipfile.Path confirms string return and identical child/nonchild behavior. This is scoped local reference evidence; the remote CPython tagged source was not acquired, and no full compatibility, model-quality or PR-conversion benefit is claimed.

Maintainer closes the issue as not planned: class-valued hookspec acceptance was unintended, restoration is rejected even with deprecation, and the entry-point-loading fix belongs downstream. This is API-intent evidence, not a claim that all regressions or undocumented callers are invalid.

The restoration PR was closed despite native regression/control validation. Retain this as an unsuccessful contribution outcome, not as evidence that passing tests establish upstream acceptance or improved discovery yield.
